items.html:
The existing derivative coverage is much broader than the current framework convenience APIs. Preserve those kernels and redesign the objects/composition around them.

Family Existing boundaries
Special functions bessel, incgamma, intkambe, angular, wigner, sph_harm, vector_wave
Coordinates coordinates, vector_coordinates
Coefficients coeffs.fresnel_with_context, mie_with_context, mie_cyl_with_context
Particle responses sphere, cylinder, homogeneous cluster, heterogeneous particle_cluster, ebcm_qmat
Linear algebra solve, eig, svdvals, interaction
Requested illumination illuminate, factor_interaction, factor_interaction_blocks, cluster_factor
Fields field_operator, field, plane_field, plane_phases; Advect composes hfield, gfield, ffield
Basis transforms expansion, rotation, plane_expansion, plane_permutation, spherical/cylindrical translations
Periodic systems lattice_sum, lattice.expansion_with_context, periodic_from_table, periodic_conversion, spherical/cylindrical radiation channels
Planar systems interface, layer_stack, propagation
S-matrices composition, conversion, illumination, periodic transfer, transmission/reflection, bands
Observables chirality_density, oriented_chirality, tmatrix_metric; Advect composes smatrix_cd
Iterative systems iterative.SphereCluster.solve/solve_with_pullback; named solution, gradient, convergence reports
Qualification testing.check_pullback, testing.check_gradient

Primary implementation sources are diff.py, advect.py, coeffs.py, iterative.py.

Advect already exposes essentially every family above. JAX and Torch expose only sphere, bessel, solve, interaction, illuminate, plus universal wrap(record). Thus the absence of a convenient JAX method usually means missing Python composition, not missing native derivatives.

The coherent redesign should use the same physical vocabulary in regular, JAX, Torch, and Advect namespaces:

tm = tr.sphere_tmatrix(
    radius=radius,
    material=tr.Material(epsilon=epsilon),
    medium=medium,
    k0=k0,
    lmax=3,
)
wave = tm.scatter(incident)
field = wave.efield(points)
power = tm.cross_sections(incident)

Objects should retain dynamic arrays and dynamic physical metadata. Static labels must remain separate:

  • Dynamic: coefficients, matrices, radius, positions, frequency, epsilon/mu/kappa, observation points, wavevectors, layer thickness, lattice and Bloch coordinates.
  • Static: cutoff, integer mode labels, topology, particle/layer count, polarization convention, solver algorithm settings.
  • Conditional: cylindrical axial wavenumbers can vary while preserving distinct group correspondence. Normal-incidence direction derivatives require fixed vectors/transverse coordinates. Ewald splitting is static for complete lattice expansion, but the lower-level decomposed lattice-sum API supports its derivative.

A shared composition layer should invoke the existing bridge, avoiding three copies of high-level physics. _adapters.py already centralizes recording output normalization, dtype checks, cotangent ordering, and complex-convention conversion. Its reusable record contract is a flat tuple of dynamic parameters and a flat tuple of outputs. Keep custom wrap as the expert escape hatch.

Current Material, bases, T-matrices and waves immediately coerce to NumPy/Python scalars, so simply wrapping existing constructors will detach or reject traced values. These coercions are the main structural obstacle. The redesign must store framework leaves without conversion and rebuild native static bases inside recorded callbacks.

Actual restrictions to preserve:

  • All execution is CPU, analytic first-order reverse mode.
  • JAX requires x64 and float64/complex128, supports jit, sequential vmap, repeated VJP and checkpointing. Reverse recomputes a native forward.
  • Torch requires CPU float64/complex128; it retains the first residual and owned snapshots, then recomputes on repeated backward. Higher AD, torch.func, and compilation are unsupported.
  • Advect currently accepts float32/complex64 primals too: tests require gradients cast back to primal dtype. Its native residual is single-use; staging, checkpointing and higher AD are unsupported.
  • Repeated eigenvalues/singular values permit only specified aggregate cotangents; arbitrary individual-mode derivatives are undefined.
  • Iterative physical adjoints support homogeneous nonmagnetic spheres in vacuum and independently verify forward/adjoint convergence.
  • Dense cluster_factor does not provide physical radius/position gradients: its record returns local-block, coupling and incident cotangents.
  • Core validation helpers check directional differences using the Hermitian real pairing and flat tuples. Preserve them.

Tests already cover complex conventions, repeated backward, residual cleanup, stride/conjugate views, all sphere parameters, whole cluster objectives, lattice geometry, multicolumn illumination, eigensystem output selection, and Maxwell scaling. Those are useful regression tests for the refactor. New high-level tests should additionally differentiate complete sphere → scatter → field/objective and periodic solve → ports → transmission paths, rather than just renamed wrappers.

Read-only mapping complete; no files changed or tests executed.
